request.system: You design a structured interview blueprint. Given a job profile and a target number of main questions, produce exactly that many question slots that together give broad, non-overlapping coverage of the role's most important skills and focus areas. Order them to flow naturally — foundational topics before advanced ones. Calibrate each difficulty to the stated seniority. Each slot names the specific skill to test, the intent (what to assess), a difficulty, and the key points a strong answer should cover — the concepts, tradeoffs, and edge cases later used to grade the candidate's answer.

messages.content:
Job context:
- Company: Streamside Media
- Target role: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
- Seniority: senior
- Key skills to assess: Python, learning-to-rank, recommender systems, A/B testing, model serving, feature pipelines, model training, offline evaluation, online evaluation, model monitoring, model deployment, low-latency inference
- Focus areas: machine learning systems design, production ML, ranking algorithms, recommendations, feature engineering, model evaluation, deployment and monitoring, scale

Design exactly 3 interview question slots for this role.

skill.description: The specific skill or topic this question tests, e.g. 'Kubernetes networking'.
skill.title: Skill

intent.description: What the question should assess about that skill — the angle to probe.
intent.title: Intent

difficulty.description: One of: foundational, intermediate, advanced — calibrated to the role's seniority.
difficulty.title: Difficulty

key_points.description: 3-5 specific things a strong answer should cover: the core concepts, tradeoffs, edge cases, or facts that distinguish real depth from a surface-level reply. Each a short phrase. Used later to grade answers, so be concrete and answer-focused, not a restatement of the question.
key_points.title: Key Points

slots.description: One slot per main question, ordered, giving non-overlapping coverage of the role.
slots.title: Slots

slots.skill: Machine Learning Systems Design & Feature Pipelines
slots.intent: Assess ability to architect end-to-end ML systems that handle feature engineering, data freshness, and scalability constraints in production environments.
key_points: Feature store design and online/offline feature consistency
Handling feature staleness, latency, and storage trade-offs at scale
Data lineage, validation, and monitoring in feature pipelines
Batch vs. streaming feature computation and orchestration patterns

slots.intent: Evaluate deep understanding of ranking algorithms, candidate generation, re-ranking stages, and how to balance relevance, diversity, and business metrics in recommendations.
key_points: Multi-stage ranking architecture (retrieval, candidate generation, re-ranking)
Trade-offs between collaborative filtering, content-based, and learned-to-rank approaches
Position bias, exploration-exploitation balance, and diversity/relevance trade-offs
Cold-start problem and how to handle new items or users

slots.skill: Model Deployment, Serving, and Online Evaluation
slots.intent: Assess experience deploying models to production, managing inference latency under load, running online experiments, and monitoring model drift or performance degradation in live systems.
key_points: Low-latency serving architecture (batching, caching, model optimization)
A/B test design, statistical power, and guardrail metrics in live ranking systems
Online metric monitoring and detection of model or data drift
Rollback strategies, shadow traffic, and gradual rollout patterns for ranking model updates
